purpose: Freeze the exact provider and model configuration for the independent A/B triage so the run is reproducible, bounded, and governance-reviewed before any data leaves the machine. This artifact records the configuration without executing it.

frozen_detector_policy.note: The detector policy and threshold are not touched by triage. Triage consumes frozen evidence bundles only.

independence_requirement.requirement: The two assessors must not share model priors. Two prompts over one model is not independence; agreement between them would measure the model, not the assessors.
independence_requirement.minimum_bar: two distinct model families, or one model with an independently sourced second assessor

observed_catalog.note: Both providers advertise the identical five models; they are mirrors, not independent sources.
observed_catalog.verified_working_note: Original observation (2026-10-08): the two DeepSeek variants are one family and cannot pair with each other. Re-probed 2026-10-27: mimo-v2.6-flash also responds, providing the distinct-family pairing.
observed_catalog.reasoning_effort_support: low, high, max for both DeepSeek models; not advertised for the other three

reprobe_2026_10_27.method: POST /chat/completions with a single-line capability prompt; the gateway requires a browser-like User-Agent and an x-opencode-session header

independence_requirement.established_basis: Two distinct model families verified responsive on 2026-10-27 through the zen/go gateway: deepseek-v4.1-flash (DeepSeek family - deepseek.com) and mimo-v2.6-flash (Xiaomi MiMo family - mimo.xiaomi.com, github.com/XiaomiMiMo). Family identities verified against vendor sources, not inferred from catalog names. Residual note: both models route through one relay gateway (opencode-go); the model families are distinct, the transport path is shared.

egress_policy.decision: APPROVED - content defensible (2026-10-08 audit) and transport approved 2026-10-27 via freeze status HUMAN_APPROVED (owner, rebuild-plan Phase 0.2)
egress_policy.audit_method: built a real EvidenceBundle from the committed fixture and inspected the exact canonical snapshot a provider would receive
egress_policy.permitted_payload: the canonical label-free EvidenceBundle snapshot produced by cluelattice.triage.snapshot.input_snapshot, which is the only object an assessor may receive
prohibited_payloads: raw CTU-13 flow records or packet payloads
repository file paths or internal identifiers beyond the snapshot fields
findings: No ground-truth label reaches the snapshot. The bundle's missing_context field states that labels are deliberately excluded, which is a statement about labels rather than a label value.
No raw payload, no file path, and no scenario identifier reaches the snapshot.
IP addresses do reach the snapshot as evidence, which is inherent: host identity is the grouping key. CTU-13 is a public, published research dataset, so these addresses are already public.
egress_policy.residual_risk: Egress of public research-dataset addresses to a third-party provider is a governance decision, not a technical one. The provider's retention and training-use terms must be recorded before the first call.
egress_policy.transport_status: IMPLEMENTED - gate now open for approved status. The provider boundary (src/cluelattice/triage/provider.py, src/cluelattice/triage/run.py) refuses any provider whose descriptor requires egress unless the freeze status is an approved value; since 2026-10-27 the status is HUMAN_APPROVED, so remote providers are permitted. No network-capable import exists in the boundary itself; the owner-approved LLM client that makes the actual calls is the next implementation stage under issue #11.

retention_terms.sequence_note: Not recorded before the first request: four capability-probe requests (single-line prompt, no project content) were sent earlier the same day under owner-approved Phase 0 probing, before this record was written. No evidence snapshot, corpus record, or dataset content has ever been sent. Recorded here as an honest sequence note.
terms: OpenCode Terms of Service (https://opencode.ai/legal/terms-of-service): content sent to third-party models is subject to that model provider's retention policy; OpenCode states it does not retain the content but cannot control third-party retention.

Go/Zen data-usage clarification (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/35102): downstream providers follow zero retention and do not use data for model training, with exceptions for free models; OpenCode's own handling of prompts in transit is not explicitly stated.
Both designated models are metered (billing_source 'go', not '-free'), so the documented free-model training exception does not apply to this pair.
retention_terms.residual_risk: Prompt content (the label-free snapshot) transits the OpenCode relay to the upstream model provider. The snapshot contents were audited on 2026-10-08 (permitted_payload/prohibited_payloads above). This remains the owner's recorded governance acceptance.

budget.basis: bounds the experiment so a runaway loop cannot consume resources before a human reviews interim output
abort_conditions: any provider error rate above 20 percent
any snapshot digest mismatch between the two roles
any response that would be stored without citations
budget.measured_spend: 0.00 USD - 4 capability-probe requests sent to the zen/go gateway on 2026-10-27 under owner-approved Phase 0 (2 returned a completion, 2 failed: one unavailable, one deprecated); single-line capability prompts only, no project, corpus, or dataset content; 0 experiment runs, 0 assessments, 0 evidence snapshots sent

unmet_conditions.detail: Owner approved on 2026-10-27 the addition of a minimal LLM client and secret handling (credential: OPENCODE_API_KEY, stored in the machine credential store, never committed) as part of rebuild-plan Phase 0.
